context.name: Context
context.audience: Anyone new to FLEX, including non-engineers
context.blurb: FLEX inside GOV.UK Once: the people it serves, its sibling systems, and the one organisation outside the boundary its request handling exchanges data with. C4 level 1 — runtime only.
context.note: 6 domains · 3 service gateways · 2 shared APIs · 277+ AWS resources in production

request.name: Request path
request.audience: On-call, and anyone tracing a live request
request.blurb: Every hop a single public request takes, numbered in reading order, and what each one checks. The turn at hop 7 is where the request leaves the public plane and re-enters FLEX through the private API.
request.note: Hops 2a and 2b both act on the viewer request at the edge — nothing in this repository fixes which of them runs first, so they are drawn side by side rather than in sequence. Hops 9a and 9b are alternatives, and one request may make several of them, in sequence or in parallel. Everything from hop 6 onwards runs inside the VPC; the tiers themselves live on the Network tab.

tables.note: Retries are opt-in and nothing on the internal path opts in, so every domain to private-API to gateway call is single-attempt.

containers.name: Containers
containers.audience: Platform engineers, and anyone reviewing a change
containers.blurb: Every separately deployable or storable part of the runtime request path, and the traffic between them. Build, deploy and alerting machinery lives on the Delivery tab. C4 level 2.
containers.note: Web ACLs, Shield and the VPC are not containers — they are policy and network attached to the boxes below, so each one's effect is a fact on the container it guards and an entry in that container's resource list. Note what is absent: FLEX owns no datastore, no queue and no event bus, so every user request is a synchronous fan-out that has to finish inside a 20 to 30 second Lambda timeout.

tables.name: The three Lambda access tiers
tables.note: All three share the rest: NODEJS_24_X, Tracing.ACTIVE, a 10-second default timeout, a log group at one year, environmentEncryption from resolveEncryptionKey() with grantDecrypt to the function, FLEX_ENVIRONMENT set to the stage, and a ResourceOwner tag at priority 200 when the function belongs to a domain. A route picks its tier with access; isolated is the default. Source: constructs/lambda/flex-*-function.ts.
rows: On, and there is no prop to turn them off

components.name: Components
components.audience: Domain teams — this is the part you write
components.blurb: C4 level 3: what a domain team actually writes, and what the platform's own libraries do with it. Every box here is FLEX code — this is the product the platform ships to its domain teams.
components.note: Two files ship a route: domains/{name}/domain.config.ts and one handler file whose path toHandlerPath derives from the route key. Route counts live on Resources, log retention and redaction patterns under Resources ▸ Observability, and the private API's access model on Resources, API layer (api-private).

network.name: Network
network.audience: Platform engineers, and network or security review
network.blurb: One VPC per persistent environment: three subnet tiers, six interface endpoints, and the two paths that actually reach the public internet.
network.note: Ephemeral PR and personal stages build no network of their own. They import the development environment's nine subnet IDs, both security groups and the API Gateway endpoint ID through addExternalExports, so everything drawn inside the VPC is shared with development.

security.name: Security
security.audience: Security review, assurance and threat modelling
security.blurb: Every control a request meets, outside in: what the edge drops, what the origin lock demands, what the token is allowed to prove, and what IAM permits once the request is inside. The permissions boundary at layer 3 is the reason the private API exists at all.
security.note: Two gaps are real and unfixed. pnpm validate:integrations filters to type: "domain", so only 6 of the 36 declared integrations are checked — the 30 gateway integrations pass CI unexamined, including local-council's two, which point at /v1/local-council/* routes the udp gateway does not define. And the authorizer's allow policy names Resource: "*" rather than the invoked method ARN.

delivery.name: Delivery
delivery.blurb: How code reaches production, and how production reaches a human when it goes wrong. Nothing on this tab is on a user's request path.
delivery.note: Two of the paths drawn here do not work today. The canary's alarm has no alarm action, and the cross-region relay's inline handler has a syntax error, so the smoke test and every us-east-1 edge alarm currently notify nobody. Both are one-line fixes.

tables.name: Every alarm, its threshold, and which topic it reaches
tables.note: 18 alarms from six constructs in constructs/alarms/. Every one sets treatMissingData: NOT_BREACHING, so silence never fires an alarm. Critical and Warning are two separate SNS topics, wired in constructs/alarms/actions.ts. The CloudFront, CloudFront Function and Shield rows are measured in us-east-1, because that is the only region those metrics are emitted to — they reach the eu-west-2 topics through the cross-region relay.
rows: Blocked requests, anomaly detection at 2 std devs

resources.name: Resources
resources.audience: Cost, audit and incident scoping — and the detail behind every badge
resources.blurb: Every AWS resource this repository creates, what configures it, and which stack owns it.
resources.note: Counts follow the stage selector in the header. They differ because domains, routes and whole stacks are gated by their environments array — and because an ephemeral PR stage reuses the development core rather than building its own. Entries whose meta reads varies carry no number, so any group total that includes one is a floor rather than a total.
